What is it like ancient times? Like the 2000s?!? Besides, what is a "fact" anyway? Who decides when a fact is or isn't correct? Facts are up to interpretation and we're told what's true and what isn't by some mysterious whatever authority somewhere. It's like how they keep telling me the sun is real. A "Giant nuclear furnace ball in space". Yeah right!  I think it's a giant light sucking up electricity for the big power companies to keep billing us or whatever. Electricity should be free cause it's a right or whatever.  Anyway bed rotting rules. Writing up these stupid descriptions as my unpaid internship for some stupid youtube channel sucks though. So this is me quietly quitting by writing a really bad intro about an ugly guy named Jack coming up with questions for his dumb, ugly boomer friends. How embarrassing. Is this what these 70 year old dudes do with their time? Back to the old folks home you bunch of bags of walking dust.</article>

items.title: MARYANN BRANDON - Editor
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 214 Maryann Brandon - Editor

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with editor Maryann Brandon (THE RISE OF SKYWALKER, THE FORCE AWAKENS, ALIAS). Maryann was recruited by NYU to enter its film program, and after graduating alongside classmates such as Spike Lee, Ang Lee, and Ernest Dickerson (Season 2, Episode 58), she found work on Bob Rafelson's BLACK WIDOW. Throughout the episode, we discuss Maryann's approach to editing, how she manages the workload on large Hollywood franchise films such as STAR WARS and STAR TREK, and her longtime working relationship with director J.J. Abrams. We learn how they first met and how she balanced editing the series ALIAS while occasionally directing the 2nd unit, and she reveals why she decided to commit to editing full time. Maryann edited the first HOW TO TRAIN YOUR DRAGON film, which we also consulted on, and we compare how different working in animation is to live action. Maryann later reflects on the reception to PASSENGERS, and we discuss her opinion on focus groups and test screenings. Plus, Maryann shares her advice for younger editors.

This episode is sponsored by Aputure & BenQ

items.title: ADAM BRICKER - Cinematographer
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 213 Adam Bricker - Cinematographer

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with cinematographer Adam Bricker (HACKS, CHEF'S TABLE, AMERICAN VANDAL). After being hosted by Adam at several Q&A's around Los Angeles, we turn the tables on him, and we ask him about his own career, learning about his journey from Chicago to Los Angeles and the many hours he put in cold-calling filmmakers on Craigslist to pitch himself as a cinematographer. We also discuss the value of having an agent as a DP, and Adam reflects on the privilege of having been able to work in Los Angeles during an extended city-wide downturn in production shoot days. Adam was also the sole cinematographer across five seasons and nearly 50 episodes on HACKS, a comedy series on HBO MAX, and he reveals how he and the other filmmakers approached shooting the show, from location scouting and prepping to grabbing the footage on the day. Adam also reflects on nailing the final shot of the series, and he shares how he endeavored to imbue a single-camera sensibility into the multi-cam show. Plus, we discuss Adam's relationship with light meters.

Recommended Viewing: HACKS

This episode is sponsored by BenQ & Aputure

items.title: Mike and Jay Talk About It Ends
items.author: RedLetterMedia
items.content: <article>Mike and Jay both enjoyed a little film called "It Ends" and wanted to have a chat about it. Often cited as having a misleading ad campaign making the film look more like a horror movie about zombies trying to get you as you drive down a road in a car, the movie is more a laid back existential thriller about the most terrifying thing of all - having to be alive with your own nasty ass. Dealing with the shock that once you leave college and head out into the real world, that life is nothing but an endless series of holidays, routines, chores and then you die.</article>

George MacKay is our special guest this week, and he’s in full dashing Austenian gentleman mode to tell Simon all about Sense and Sensibility. He plays Edward Ferrars, the handsome and thoroughly upstanding chap who catches the eye of Daisy Edgar-Jones’ Elinor Dashwood. He talks about bringing this Austen classic up to date, three decades on from Ang Lee’s classic screen version starring Emma Thompson, Kate Winslet and Hugh Grant.  
 
Mark reviews the film, plus another three big movies hitting cinema screens this week. There’s Heart of the Beast, a survival thriller starring Brad Pitt as an ex-special forces soldier living on society’s inhospitable margins alongside his ex-service dog. Plus we’ll finally get Mark’s verdict on Her Private Hell, the latest neon-soaked feature from recent Take guest Nicolas Winding Refn. Last but certainly not least, Boorman and the Devil - a documentary about the making of the colossally unsuccessful sequel Exorcist II: The Heretic. Surely this one is Kermode catnip. 
 
Plus the weekly joy (and/or pain) of the Laughter Lift, and of your consistently excellent correspondence. Keep it coming!

items.title: MOTHER MARY - with David Lowery
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 212 MOTHER MARY - with David Lowery

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, director David Lowery (Season 2, Episode 60) returns to discuss his latest film, MOTHER MARY, now available to stream at home. Throughout the episode, we discuss the making of the movie, and topics include: the origin of the two lead characters, shooting the dialogue-heavy script, the evolution of the concert footage, and filming the bulk of the movie in 2023 and the remainder in 2024. We learn how the "ghost" was visualized and captured practically, where the supernatural elements of the movie came from, how actress Anne Hathaway prepared for her character's elaborate dance choreography, and why the film was shot in Germany even though it's set in England. David also shares how the process of developing MOTHER MARY differed and mirrored the development of his other films. In addition to learning how David filmed the movie, we also discuss how much work was done in post, and David reveals the level of invisible VFX work in the final cut. Plus, David shares some information about his next project.

Recommended Viewing: MOTHER MARY

This episode is sponsored by Aputure
